scope: On every positive periodic SU(2) spatial lattice, a seam configuration with arbitrary holonomy q has every spatial plaquette holonomy equal to the identity, while its actual gauge-invariant winding loop equals the real character of q. The q=1 and q=-1 configurations are gauge inequivalent, including at even periods. No function of the complete spatial plaquette holonomies can reconstruct this winding observable, whose variance under the original physical ground law is strictly positive at each finite cutoff. The central seam twist J multiplies seam links by -1. It is a continuous Haar-preserving involution commuting with gauge transformations and preserving every spatial plaquette holonomy, the simultaneous kinetic action, the raw Wilson kernel, the original normalized physical ground, and its stationary integrals. The winding loop is J-odd. Every continuous real source decomposes into f_plus=(f+f composed with J)/2 and f_minus=(f-f composed with J)/2. For physical sources both parts remain gauge invariant. They are orthogonal under the actual ground law, and their mass, variance and actual transfer loss split exactly. Both parts commute with the normalized raw transfer; on invariant sources this is the original full physical transition by the existing step_full identification. Defining E_J(f)=integral (f(Ju)-f(u))^2 d(pi), the exact identity is Var(f)=Var(f_plus)+E_J(f)/4. In particular every odd source, including the nonzero physical winding loop, has Var(f)=E_J(f)/4, with coefficient independent of coupling and volume. The response is a whole-seam center flip, not the earlier small single-link response form or a new physical time step. No comparison of E_J(Pf) with actual transfer loss is proved. Every plaquette-based weighting leaves the winding loop centered; this is an integral identity, not a conditional-variance lower bound. A nonconstant physical plaquette has zero twist response and positive ground variance when n>1, formally ruling out all-physical coercivity from this one global response alone. Center-even global holonomy modes can also remain. The complete distant mixed-ground sum, bridge-complement estimate, combined global coercivity, physical mass gap and nonzero continuum construction remain unproved. All twelve full Clay requirements stay open.
